name: core.openwop.workflows.approvals
description: Real-work workflow pack (RFC 0013, ADR 0198) — the Approvals cluster, the single most-used enterprise automation shape (Power Automate's #1 template is a sign-off flow with ~3.35M instantiations): Request Sign-off (an open gate any team member can approve — the zero-config marquee) and Two-Stage Sign-off (an ordered approval chain: stage two is only asked after stage one approves — sequential chains are DAG composition, not a new primitive). Gates support quorum (requiredApprovals), named approvers (approverRefs), and out-of-office delegation (an approver's active delegation lets their delegate act, counted as ONE identity — ADR 0198). All tenant values are run parameters (replay-deterministic).
author: openwop

chains.label: Request Sign-off
chains.description: The classic sign-off: describe what needs approval, get a crisp summary card, and any team member signs off (or rejects) — then the decision comes back to you as a notification. Zero configuration; approvers on leave are covered automatically by their delegations.

item.description: What needs sign-off (a document, a change, a request — paste or describe it).

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: Write a crisp sign-off card for this item: WHAT is being approved (1 line), WHY it matters, and what saying yes commits us to. Under 120 words, no fluff. Item: {{params.item}}

decision.description: The sign-off decision with the summary it was made on.

chains.label: Two-Stage Sign-off
chains.description: An ordered approval chain: stage one (e.g. the manager) approves first; only then is stage two (e.g. compliance) asked. Name each stage's approver by id to route the request to them — or leave a stage blank to open it to the whole team. Approvers on leave are covered automatically by their delegations.

stageOneApprover.description: Stage-one approver id (blank = any team member).

stageTwoApprover.description: Stage-two approver id (blank = any team member).

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: Write a crisp sign-off card for this item: WHAT is being approved (1 line), WHY it matters, and what saying yes commits us to. Under 120 words. Item: {{params.item}}

decision.description: Both stage decisions with the summary they were made on.
